name: io.github.ABCastor/borgo
title: Borgo
description: Compare cities to live in on open, sourced data: take-home pay, rent, visas, climate, safety.

tools.name: search_cities
tools.description: Find cities already in the dataset (the snapshot and places fetched before) by name, alias or id, optionally within one country. Returns ids for the other tools, how many match and whether more do. This server holds Borgo's published cities; any other place needs the local server (npx -y @abcastor/borgo mcp) and its fetch_city.

query.description: Name, alias or id; empty lists every city

limit.description: Default 10 for a query, 100 for the full list

tools.name: get_city
tools.description: One city's figures, each with source, period, geographic level and licence; daylight; the take-home pay model; whether each person in a household may live and work there, with the rules checked; links to sources we may not copy, and Borgo's generic quality-of-life index with its fixed weights. Compact by default (figures with a value, long series counted); pass metrics for a few figures, detail "full" for everything.

passports.description: Optional: each person's passports, e.g. [['US']] or [['IT'],['US','IE']]: who may live and work there

rights.description: Optional: each person's rights to live and work that are not citizenship, in the same order as passports, e.g. [[{kind:'permanent',where:'DE'}]]

kind.description: permanent: Permanent residence (a green card, Niederlassungserlaubnis, EU long-term residence, indefinite leave to remain); settled: Settled status (the UK's EU Settlement Scheme); residence: Residence permit (a residence card as a family member, a permit for self-employment); work: Work visa or permit (an H-1B, a Skilled Worker visa, a Critical Skills permit); blue-card: EU Blue Card (the EU's permit for highly qualified work); other: Other right to live and work (a treaty right, a youth mobility visa)

where.description: Where it holds: a country, ISO alpha-2 (DE), or a free-movement area id (EEA) for a right granted across it

until.description: Its last valid day, YYYY-MM-DD; leave out for a right without an end

work.description: false when it allows living there but not working; default true

metrics.description: Only these metric ids, e.g. ['rent_1bed','pm25']; list_metrics_and_sources kind "metrics" lists them

tools.name: compare_cities
tools.description: Rank any number of cities for a person or household: a verdict, the score out of 100 from their weights with points and reasons per line, must-pass lines as pass, fail or unknown, each earner's take-home pay and what is left after rent and spending, who can move there, how the set was scored, and what to add next. Every figure carries its source and period. Compact by default; detail "full" adds every tax line, childcare, health, leave and break-even.

cities.description: City ids (e.g. turin-it) or names in any common spelling (Turin, Torino, 'Paris, FR'); a name two places share needs its country

work.description: The person's kind of work, only if they said it: software (Software and IT), engineering (Engineering, not software), science (Research and science), medicine (Doctors and dentists), nursing (Nursing and care), teaching (Teaching and education), finance (Finance and accounting), law (Law), marketing (Marketing, design and media), office (Office and administration), sales (Sales and retail), hospitality (Hospitality and food), trades (Construction and trades), transport (Transport and logistics), public (Public sector), management (Management), founder (Founding a company). Adds what people in that work earn there and how many jobs its field holds to Work and ambition, and shares the group's weight by the kind's recipe (founder: young companies, developers, graduates); each city then says why in plain sentences (work). Leave out for the same Work and ambition as everyone

weights.description: Weight 0-100 per criterion, on top of the preset. Criteria: money_left, living_cost, right_to_live, nice_days, winter_light, sunshine, dry_days, clean_air, safety, long_life, health_costs, childcare, family_leave, happiness, builders, field_pay, field_jobs, young_companies, time_zone, flight_home, airport, public_transport, rail, short_commute, cycling, walkable, active_commute, way_out, sea, mountains, green, internet, english, international, doctors, jobs, degrees, developers, qol, clean_government, politics, abortion, couples_law, founders_run, coworking, climbing, swimming, beach, run_ride, muggy, grey, hot_nights, heat, snow, wind

only.description: Score only these criteria; every other line gets weight 0 (each listed one keeps its `weights` value, else 100). For a one-line question: only ["nice_days"] with comfort {min:20,max:28}

detail.description: "summary" (default): verdict, ranking, weighted lines with citations, money in brief, who can move there, notes, required unknowns and next inputs. "full": every line, tax line and source, for programs

limit.description: How many ranked cities to describe in the summary (default 10); the ranking counts the rest

household.description: Everyone moving, you first. Anyone after you can bring their own pay; a spouse counts for joint filing even with none

passports.description: ISO alpha-2 codes, e.g. ['IT','US'], if known. Leave out when you do not know them: that person's right to live there is then reported as not checked, never as needing a visa

entryRoutes.description: Country to route id, only if conditions are confirmed: GB gb-ancestry (Commonwealth citizenship, eligible grandparent, support and work), gb-skilled (sponsored eligible job, salary and English); US us-h1b (cap-subject employer petition). Rough guide, not legal advice; other routes are not checked.

rights.description: Rights to live and work this person holds that are not citizenship, only if they told you: permanent residence (a green card, indefinite leave to remain), settled status, a residence permit, a work visa, an EU Blue Card. Each has a kind, where it holds (a country or a free-movement area id such as EEA), and its last valid day if it ends. A permit counts until that day; one that ended, or bars work (work: false), does not

until.description: Its last valid day, YYYY-MM-DD; leave out for a right without an end

work.description: false when it allows living there but not working; default true

regimeConfirmations.description: This person's answers to newcomer-regime conditions no dataset can check, by condition id (list_metrics_and_sources kind "regimes"), e.g. {"nl-recruited-abroad": true}. Only what the person told you

age.description: Age in years: age-dependent tax (youth relief, care insurance), pension caps, paid leave, newcomer regimes

salary.description: Not for the first person (use `salary`): this person's gross yearly pay, the same everywhere

currency.description: ISO 4217, e.g. EUR, GBP, USD. Default: the display currency

salaryByCity.description: Not for the first person: this person's gross per city, keyed by city id or name

currency.description: ISO 4217, e.g. EUR, GBP, USD. Default: the display currency

pension.description: This person's pension share of gross, 0.05 = 5%

spouse.description: Married to (or registered partner of) the first person: joint filing where the country has it, applied when it is required or cheaper

relation.description: Partner decides couple vs single-parent childcare

yearsSinceResident.description: Whole years since last tax resident there, by ISO alpha-2, or 'never': for newcomer regimes

regimes.description: Not for the first person (use `regimes`): newcomer regimes this person chose, ISO alpha-2 -> regime id, checked against this person's own facts and confirmations; a scenario until they meet every condition

salary.description: Your gross yearly salary, the same everywhere

currency.description: ISO 4217, e.g. EUR, GBP, USD. Default: the display currency

pension.description: Share of your gross paid into a pension, 0.05 = 5%: it leaves take-home pay and is shown as saving, not cost. Tax relief is modelled for CA (RRSP), CH (pillar 3a), CZ (pension savings (penzijní spoření)), DE (occupational pension (Entgeltumwandlung)), EE (third pillar), ES (plan de pensiones), FR (PER (plan d'épargne retraite)), GB (workplace or personal pension), HU (voluntary pension fund), IE (occupational pension or PRSA), IT (fondo pensione), JP (iDeCo), NL (workplace pension), NO (IPS (individual pension savings)), PT (PPR), SG (SRS), US (401(k)); elsewhere it is not modelled and the share is counted as saving with no relief (each city's money says which)

children.description: Children's ages: childcare after public support for under-6s (OECD), child credits and allowances where the tax uses them, health for each person

paidChildcare.description: Whether the household pays for childcare for its children under 6 (default true). false: no childcare cost is counted. Ask when it matters: the default prices full-time care for an OECD reference household

childcareCost.description: What the household actually pays for childcare in a city, after support, keyed by city id or name, in the city's currency, with per "month" or "year": replaces the OECD reference figure

amount.description: Amount, in the city's own currency

per.description: What the amount is for: a month or a year

healthPremium.description: The household's health insurance premium bought outside pay (US, CH, NL), keyed by city id or name, in the city's currency, with per "month" or "year" (a year is counted as a twelfth a month)

amount.description: Amount, in the city's own currency

per.description: What the amount is for: a month or a year

regimes.description: Newcomer tax regime per country, ISO alpha-2 -> regime id from list_metrics_and_sources. None counts unless named here; a named one is a scenario until the person's facts and confirmations meet every condition

salaryByCity.description: Gross yearly salary per city (offers or estimates), keyed by city id or name

currency.description: ISO 4217, e.g. EUR, GBP, USD. Default: the display currency

displayCurrency.description: Currency to show amounts in (default: the salary's, else EUR)

spending.description: Monthly spending on everything except housing, childcare and health, which are counted separately

currency.description: ISO 4217, e.g. EUR, GBP, USD. Default: the display currency

homeCity.description: Where you spend this today; default: the first city

savings.description: Savings in the display currency, for runway

comfort.description: Weather: what a nice day is, for criterion nice_days: the daytime temperature range, °C (default 18-30 on the feels-like temperature; basis "air" uses the air in the shade), then the tests a day must pass. Only the person's own words: rain and sky are on unless they drop them; humidity, wind and daylight only when they ask. All from ERA5 (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0) and the latitude

dry.description: Under 1 mm of rain from 8 am to 8 pm (default true; false lets rain through)

clear.description: At most half the sky clouded on average from 8 am to 8 pm, the sunshine test (default true)

notMuggy.description: Not muggy: the day's mean dew point under 18 °C (default false)

calm.description: Calm: the daytime wind under 20 km/h on average (default false)

daylight.description: At least this many hours of daylight, from the latitude (default none)

normalise.description: Default absolute: fixed city-local scores. Relative is opt-in: adding cities can change other scores, gap handling and the shared money basis.

missing.description: In fixed scoring, missing lines do not count for that city. Only with opt-in relative scoring: lowest scores gaps at the lowest compared score, worst at 0, skip drops the line for all. Money is never imputed

overrides.description: Your own numbers: city -> metric id -> value; money in the city's currency. health_premium is the household's premium a month (prefer healthPremium, which takes the period); childcare_cost is the household's own childcare a month (prefer childcareCost); childcare_net_couple_1 and similar replace the OECD reference figure, a year

dealBreakers.description: Must-pass criterion ids, e.g. right_to_live, money_left: a city fails, passes, or is unknown (no figure, no passport or other right given); unknown ranks after every city that passes

stances.description: Where the person stands on the position lines, which score a place by its distance from them: politics 0 (left) to 10 (right); abortion 0 not allowed or only to save her life, 1 also for her health or after rape, 2 also on social or economic grounds, 3 on request in the first weeks only, 4 on request to 10 weeks or later; couples_law 0 criminalised (same-sex relations a crime), 1 legal with no union in law, 2 civil union or partnership, 3 marriage. Pass only what the person told you or what you know they hold; never guess. A stance counts once its line has a weight (they are 0 by default)

personal.description: Your own 1-5 lines, scores keyed by city

taxTweaks.description: Per-country tax tweaks keyed by ISO alpha-2

taxableShare.description: Share of gross that is taxable, e.g. 0.5 under an impatriate regime

flatRate.description: Flat income tax rate replacing the schedule, e.g. 0.24

noSocialContributions.description: You pay none of the country's employee social contributions, e.g. a foreigner on a Singapore Employment Pass pays no CPF

tools.name: rank_cities
tools.description: List known cities by any scalar/monthly metric, any priority recipe (nice days under your definition, money left with salary and spending), or your overall score. Compose inclusive metric/priority ranges, geographic and population filters and established household rights. Every row names its sources and periods. Gaps and unknown filters never pass as zero. Returns an in-chat bar chart, Equal Earth map or weather month strips, plus a markdown fallback. Defaults: descending, 20 results; rent usually needs ascending. Money uses one display currency, default EUR or salary currency. Use compare_cities for the full explanation of finalists.

regimeConfirmations.description: This person's answers to newcomer-regime conditions no dataset can check, by condition id (list_metrics_and_sources kind "regimes"), e.g. {"nl-recruited-abroad": true}. Only what the person told you

age.description: Age in years: age-dependent tax (youth relief, care insurance), pension caps, paid leave, newcomer regimes

salary.description: Not for the first person (use `salary`): this person's gross yearly pay, the same everywhere

currency.description: ISO 4217, e.g. EUR, GBP, USD. Default: the display currency

salaryByCity.description: Not for the first person: this person's gross per city, keyed by city id or name

currency.description: ISO 4217, e.g. EUR, GBP, USD. Default: the display currency

pension.description: This person's pension share of gross, 0.05 = 5%

spouse.description: Married to (or registered partner of) the first person: joint filing where the country has it, applied when it is required or cheaper

relation.description: Partner decides couple vs single-parent childcare

yearsSinceResident.description: Whole years since last tax resident there, by ISO alpha-2, or 'never': for newcomer regimes

regimes.description: Not for the first person (use `regimes`): newcomer regimes this person chose, ISO alpha-2 -> regime id, checked against this person's own facts and confirmations; a scenario until they meet every condition

salary.description: Your gross yearly salary, the same everywhere

currency.description: ISO 4217, e.g. EUR, GBP, USD. Default: the display currency

pension.description: Share of your gross paid into a pension, 0.05 = 5%: it leaves take-home pay and is shown as saving, not cost. Tax relief is modelled for CA (RRSP), CH (pillar 3a), CZ (pension savings (penzijní spoření)), DE (occupational pension (Entgeltumwandlung)), EE (third pillar), ES (plan de pensiones), FR (PER (plan d'épargne retraite)), GB (workplace or personal pension), HU (voluntary pension fund), IE (occupational pension or PRSA), IT (fondo pensione), JP (iDeCo), NL (workplace pension), NO (IPS (individual pension savings)), PT (PPR), SG (SRS), US (401(k)); elsewhere it is not modelled and the share is counted as saving with no relief (each city's money says which)

children.description: Children's ages: childcare after public support for under-6s (OECD), child credits and allowances where the tax uses them, health for each person

paidChildcare.description: Whether the household pays for childcare for its children under 6 (default true). false: no childcare cost is counted. Ask when it matters: the default prices full-time care for an OECD reference household

childcareCost.description: What the household actually pays for childcare in a city, after support, keyed by city id or name, in the city's currency, with per "month" or "year": replaces the OECD reference figure

amount.description: Amount, in the city's own currency

per.description: What the amount is for: a month or a year

healthPremium.description: The household's health insurance premium bought outside pay (US, CH, NL), keyed by city id or name, in the city's currency, with per "month" or "year" (a year is counted as a twelfth a month)

amount.description: Amount, in the city's own currency

per.description: What the amount is for: a month or a year

regimes.description: Newcomer tax regime per country, ISO alpha-2 -> regime id from list_metrics_and_sources. None counts unless named here; a named one is a scenario until the person's facts and confirmations meet every condition

salaryByCity.description: Gross yearly salary per city (offers or estimates), keyed by city id or name

currency.description: ISO 4217, e.g. EUR, GBP, USD. Default: the display currency

displayCurrency.description: Currency to show amounts in (default: the salary's, else EUR)

spending.description: Monthly spending on everything except housing, childcare and health, which are counted separately

currency.description: ISO 4217, e.g. EUR, GBP, USD. Default: the display currency

homeCity.description: Where you spend this today; default: the first city

savings.description: Savings in the display currency, for runway

comfort.description: Weather: what a nice day is, for criterion nice_days: the daytime temperature range, °C (default 18-30 on the feels-like temperature; basis "air" uses the air in the shade), then the tests a day must pass. Only the person's own words: rain and sky are on unless they drop them; humidity, wind and daylight only when they ask. All from ERA5 (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0) and the latitude

dry.description: Under 1 mm of rain from 8 am to 8 pm (default true; false lets rain through)

clear.description: At most half the sky clouded on average from 8 am to 8 pm, the sunshine test (default true)

notMuggy.description: Not muggy: the day's mean dew point under 18 °C (default false)

calm.description: Calm: the daytime wind under 20 km/h on average (default false)

daylight.description: At least this many hours of daylight, from the latitude (default none)

normalise.description: Default absolute: fixed city-local scores. Relative is opt-in: adding cities can change other scores, gap handling and the shared money basis.

missing.description: In fixed scoring, missing lines do not count for that city. Only with opt-in relative scoring: lowest scores gaps at the lowest compared score, worst at 0, skip drops the line for all. Money is never imputed

overrides.description: Your own numbers: city -> metric id -> value; money in the city's currency. health_premium is the household's premium a month (prefer healthPremium, which takes the period); childcare_cost is the household's own childcare a month (prefer childcareCost); childcare_net_couple_1 and similar replace the OECD reference figure, a year

dealBreakers.description: Must-pass criterion ids, e.g. right_to_live, money_left: a city fails, passes, or is unknown (no figure, no passport or other right given); unknown ranks after every city that passes

stances.description: Where the person stands on the position lines, which score a place by its distance from them: politics 0 (left) to 10 (right); abortion 0 not allowed or only to save her life, 1 also for her health or after rape, 2 also on social or economic grounds, 3 on request in the first weeks only, 4 on request to 10 weeks or later; couples_law 0 criminalised (same-sex relations a crime), 1 legal with no union in law, 2 civil union or partnership, 3 marriage. Pass only what the person told you or what you know they hold; never guess. A stance counts once its line has a weight (they are 0 by default)

personal.description: Your own 1-5 lines, scores keyed by city

taxTweaks.description: Per-country tax tweaks keyed by ISO alpha-2

taxableShare.description: Share of gross that is taxable, e.g. 0.5 under an impatriate regime

flatRate.description: Flat income tax rate replacing the schedule, e.g. 0.24

noSocialContributions.description: You pay none of the country's employee social contributions, e.g. a foreigner on a Singapore Employment Pass pays no CPF

tools.name: net_pay
tools.description: Take-home pay for a gross yearly salary in a country (and region or city, for regional and municipal taxes), with every tax line, the model's caveats and its official sources. Takes age, children, a pension share, a newcomer regime, and a partner (joint filing for a married couple where the country has it).

country.description: ISO alpha-2 or name; optional when city is given

city.description: City id or name; sets country, region and municipal taxes

region.description: ISO 3166-2 subdivision, e.g. US-CA, GB-SCT, IT-21

currency.description: Currency of gross; default the country's

taxableShare.description: Share of gross that is taxable, e.g. 0.5 under an impatriate regime

flatRate.description: Flat income tax rate replacing the schedule, e.g. 0.24

noSocialContributions.description: You pay none of the country's employee social contributions, e.g. a foreigner on a Singapore Employment Pass pays no CPF

age.description: Age in years, where the tax uses it

children.description: Children's ages, for child credits and allowances

regime.description: A newcomer regime id for this country (list_metrics_and_sources kind "regimes")

partner.description: A second earner in the same household

gross.description: Their gross yearly salary, in the same currency as gross; 0 for a spouse with no pay

spouse.description: Married or registered partners: joint filing where the country has it

tools.name: list_metrics_and_sources
tools.description: What the dataset holds: scoring lines with their scales and default weights, metrics with coverage, sources with licences, take-home pay models, newcomer regimes with each condition's id, presets, and the link-only sources. Pass kind for one part (kind "regimes", country "NL" lists the Dutch regimes and their conditions).

kind.description: One part only; leave out for everything

country.description: ISO alpha-2, with kind taxModels or regimes

tools.name: methodology
tools.description: How scores, weights, must-pass lines, missing data, the money model, the right to live and the open-data rule work, with every scale.

tools.name: list_sources
tools.description: The curated list of sources: what each measures (with a plain definition), coverage, licence, whether it may be redistributed, how it is fetched (endpoint, CORS, key) and who vetted it, plus link-only pages such as Numbeo and WeatherSpark. Filter by metric or country; pass a place to get the publisher's page for it.

metric.description: Metric id, e.g. pm25, rent_1bed, sunshine_hours

country.description: ISO alpha-2: only sources covering this country

city.description: A city id or name in the dataset, to fill in each publisher's page for it

tools.name: community_figures
tools.description: Figures people report for themselves about a place on Borgo, after automated review: rent by bedrooms and area, everyday prices, take-home pay by kind of work and a 1 to 5 rating of living there, each with its median (a rating: mean), middle half from 3 entries, count, months and the official figure beside it where one exists. Community data, CC BY 4.0; never mixed into official figures or scores. Covers the snapshot's cities and the towns on Borgo's map.

tools.name: submit_figures
tools.description: Send what the person pays and earns where they live to Borgo's open community data (published rounded under CC BY 4.0, no name or address kept; an automated review holds amounts far from others' or the official figure). Without confirm it sends nothing and returns the draft with its privacy note: show both to the person. Call again with confirm true only after they said yes to these exact figures, and only figures they gave you as their own, never estimates or figures read on another site. The answer carries a removal code for them to keep.

amount.description: What they pay a month, without bills, in the place's currency

bedrooms.description: 0: Studio; 1: 1 bedroom; 2: 2 bedrooms; 3: 3 or more bedrooms

prices.description: What they pay for everyday things, in the place's currency

meal.description: Meal at an inexpensive restaurant, one meal

cappuccino.description: Cappuccino in a café, one cup

transit.description: Monthly public transport pass, a month

amount.description: What they take home a month after tax

occupation.description: software: Software and IT; engineering: Engineering, not software; science: Research and science; medicine: Doctors and dentists; nursing: Nursing and care; teaching: Teaching and education; finance: Finance and accounting; law: Law; marketing: Marketing, design and media; office: Office and administration; sales: Sales and retail; hospitality: Hospitality and food; trades: Construction and trades; transport: Transport and logistics; public: Public sector; management: Management; other: Other work

rating.description: Living there, all things considered, 1 poor to 5 excellent

currency.description: ISO 4217; must be the place's own (checked)

confirm.description: true only after the person agreed to send these exact figures

tools.name: remove_figures
tools.description: Delete a submission the person sent, with the removal code it gave them.
